claims.text: Dynamic mechanical behavior across temperature and strain-rate regimes in Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by elastic strain-induced localized amorphization.
Local crystalline regions transform into an amorphous state when elastic strain reaches a critical threshold.
Formation of the amorphous state impedes dislocation nucleation.
Formation of the amorphous state impedes dislocation motion.
The target material is equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn has a primarily single-phase FCC microstructure.
In related high-entropy alloys, amorphization begins at an elastic strain of approximately 10%.
Local atomic-environment inhomogeneity depresses dislocation nucleation and is associated with elastic strain-induced amorphization.
Local atomic inhomogeneity triggers an elastic instability that produces partial amorphization in FeNiCrMn.
The deformation-induced amorphous phase is transient.
Partial amorphization redistributes stress.
Partial amorphization enhances strain hardening.
Amorphization-mediated stress redistribution and strain hardening sustain the strength-ductility balance across loading conditions.
The onset of amorphization will correspond to a distinct transition in the stress-strain curve.
The amorphization-associated transition will occur at lower strain at higher strain rates.
The amorphization-associated transition will occur at lower strain at lower temperatures.
A conventional FCC alloy lacking the proposed elastic instability would deform predominantly through dislocation-mediated plasticity without localized amorphization.
The proposed mechanism applies to solidified FeNiCrMn with a relatively homogeneous initial microstructure.
Significant pre-existing defects may diminish the influence of elastic strain-induced amorphization.
Competing hardening mechanisms in multiphase FeNiCrMn may diminish the influence of elastic strain-induced amorphization.
